title: A Power Plant on an Underwater Volcano Made Net-Positive Electricity, a First
summary: Seattle startup Endurance Energy landed a 3-ton power plant on an underwater volcano 300 miles off Oregon and generated more electricity than it consumed, the first net-positive run of subsea geothermal power. The team also drilled what it calls the world's first offshore geothermal well, a 52-foot borehole flowing at 260°C nearly a mile down.

title: A Table-Mounted Surgical Robot Completed Its First Human Surgery in Toronto
summary: Revolve Surgical's arm, which mounts to the operating table rather than needing a dedicated room, completed its first human appendectomy at St. Michael's Hospital on Oct 1. It has Health Canada investigational approval and US FDA premarket clearance, and aims to cost a fraction of seven-figure systems like da Vinci.

title: Surgeons in New Delhi Operate on Patients in Colombo in Sri Lanka's First Robotic Telesurgeries
summary: Two patients at Kings Hospital Colombo were operated on by surgeons working a robotic console more than 3,000 km away in New Delhi, a first for Sri Lanka. Both procedures finished without the on-site team needing to step in, pointing to a future where specialist surgery reaches patients far from big-city hospitals.

title: 85,000 California Home Batteries Team Up for a Record 745 MW Grid Save
summary: During an October heat wave, more than 85,000 Tesla Powerwalls plus Sunrun home batteries discharged together for a record 745 MW virtual power plant event, bigger than most gas peaker plants in the state. Homeowners got paid for helping the grid through the evening peak.

title: CRISPR Chip Names the Bacteria Behind Hard-to-Diagnose Lung Infections in Hours, Not Weeks
summary: Tulane and UNC researchers built CANDI, a CRISPR microfluidic chip that identifies 15 nontuberculous mycobacteria species from patient samples in about 3.5 hours, work that culture tests need four to six weeks to do. In 230 clinical samples it matched the right species 97.3% of the time, which means patients can start the right treatment far sooner.

title: AI Cameras and New Satellites Are Spotting California Wildfires Before People Do
summary: ALERTCalifornia's network of nearly 1,300 AI-watched cameras detected just over half of the state's wildfires before any human reported them this past summer. California has also launched the first three FireSat satellites, the start of a constellation built to catch fires while they are still the size of a schoolyard.

title: A Blood Sensor Sniffs Out Parkinson's Markers in 40 Minutes
summary: KAUST and Oxford researchers built an electronic blood sensor that measures three forms of alpha-synuclein at once, the protein signatures tied to Parkinson's, in about 40 minutes. In a blinded test it separated disease profiles from healthy controls with 87.7% accuracy, an encouraging step toward earlier diagnosis from a simple blood draw.

title: Waymo Robotaxis Have Prevented an Estimated 841 Injury Crashes
summary: Across 271 million rider-only miles through June 2026, Waymo reports 95% fewer serious-injury crashes and 82% fewer injury crashes than human benchmarks, adding up to an estimated 841 injury crashes that never happened. Cyclist and pedestrian injury crashes fell even further, down 86% and 93%.

title: First Patients Get an Under-the-Skin Implant That Puts Prosthetic Arms Under Muscle Control
summary: Two patients in Melbourne are the first to receive Phantom Neuro's Phantom X, a slim implant that sits under the skin of the forearm and turns muscle signals into prosthetic arm commands. The outpatient-style procedure took about an hour, and early users report smoother, more reliable control than surface electrodes give.

title: Solar Power Keeps Vaccines Cold and Classrooms Lit on Timor-Leste's Atauro Island
summary: A solar system handed over in July now gives Vila Maumeta's health centre, primary school and community centre power around the clock, ending the blackouts that once destroyed vaccine stocks. The village's 516 households sit on a boat-only island, and staff were trained to maintain the system themselves.

title: A Fingerprint-Locked Cabinet Makes Controlled Drugs Safer at Pinderfields Hospital
summary: Pinderfields Hospital in Wakefield has installed an automated dispensing cabinet for controlled drugs that opens only by fingerprint after a prescription check, with guiding lights that cut picking errors. Pharmacy staff say it is already saving time and freeing ward teams to spend more of it with patients.

title: Self-Balancing Exoskeleton Eve Gets FDA Clearance to Walk People Home
summary: Wandercraft's Eve is the first self-balancing personal exoskeleton cleared by the FDA, letting people with spinal cord injuries stand and walk at home with no crutches or walker. In its clearance study, 87.5% of users completed everyday tasks like opening doors and cooking, and US sales have begun.

title: Drones Now Carry Children's Pathology Samples Across London for Great Ormond Street
summary: Matternet drones working with Apian have started flying pediatric pathology samples from Great Ormond Street Hospital to nearby labs, cutting urgent delivery times by up to 90% compared with London road traffic. The London network has now flown more than 13,000 clinical items since 2024.

title: One Robot Printer and a Crew of Three Built Europe's Largest 3D-Printed Housing Project
summary: At Skovsporet in Holstebro, Denmark, a single COBOD BOD3 printer and a three-person crew printed 36 student apartments across six buildings, finishing one six-apartment building in five working days. The homes came in within Denmark's affordable-housing budget cap, kept 90% of the site's trees, and have already welcomed their first residents.

title: Two Surgeons Share One Robot in Japan's First Clinical Remote Robotic Surgeries
summary: Surgeons at Hirosaki University Hospital and Tsugaru General Hospital have jointly operated the hinotori robot on five bowel cancer patients since August, with one doctor at the patient's side and a second guiding the same robot from 30 km away. All five surgeries succeeded, and the model is aimed squarely at rural hospitals short on specialists.

title: Solar Clinics in Uganda Are Attending Twice as Many Births
summary: An analysis of a decade of data from Let There Be Light International's solar-electrified clinics in Uganda found 11.5 extra operating hours a day, about 49 more patients a week, and attended births up 107%. Reliable light after dark is what lets midwives deliver babies safely through the night.

title: Half a Million Wolbachia Mosquitoes Take Flight Over Barcelona to Fight Dengue
summary: More than half a million male mosquitoes carrying the wolbachia bacterium have been released in Barcelona, the first large-scale release of its kind in Europe. Males are sorted by AI image recognition and their matings produce eggs that never hatch; in Singapore the same approach cut dengue cases by about 70%.

title: Google's Retinal AI Has Now Screened More Than a Million Patients for Diabetic Eye Disease
summary: ARDA, Google's diabetic retinopathy screening AI, has passed one million patients screened through partner clinics at Aravind Eye Care in India, Rajavithi Hospital in Thailand and Lions Outback Vision in Australia. The screenings run at no cost to patients, with a goal of six million across India and Thailand within ten years.

title: Solar Tablets Bring Adaptive Lessons to 57,000 Tanzanian Primary Schoolers
summary: MsingiTEK has put solar-powered adaptive-learning tablets into 250 public primary schools across five Tanzanian regions, reaching more than 57,000 children in grades 1 to 3. Teachers report better attendance and stronger reading, writing and counting, and the programme is on its way to 500 schools and 120,000 students.

title: A Suitcase Robot Guides Visually Impaired Walkers Through Tokyo
summary: A suitcase-shaped AI robot developed by Japan's Miraikan science museum is guiding visually impaired people through Tokyo's Toranomon Hills in a month-long public trial, using cameras and sensors to steer around obstacles. Its built-in chatbot can also answer questions about shops and routes along the way.

title: A Night Robot Fights Vineyard Mildew With Light Instead of Fungicide
summary: Saga Robotics' Thorvald robots roll through vineyards and strawberry fields at night, zapping powdery mildew with UV-C light so growers can spray far less fungicide. In 2026 the robots are protecting about 2,500 acres of California vineyards and an estimated 30% of the UK's tabletop strawberry crop, and TIME has named Thorvald one of its Best Inventions of 2026.

title: Solar Panels Over California Canals Cut Evaporation by Up to 70%
summary: Project Nexus, a 1.6 MW pilot covering Turlock Irrigation District canals with solar panels, measured evaporation reductions of 50 to 70% and 85% less algae growth over a full irrigation season, while the water below kept the panels cooler and more productive. Covering California's canal network could one day save an estimated 63 billion gallons a year.

title: A Palm-Sized TB Test Reads a Tongue Swab in 30 Minutes
summary: The battery-powered MiniDock MTB delivers molecular tuberculosis results in about 30 minutes from a simple tongue swab, matching the accuracy of hospital lab tests in a New England Journal of Medicine study. Named one of TIME's Best Inventions of 2026, it is now being introduced in 13 countries with support from the Global Fund.

title: A 110-Story Floating Turbine Is Feeding an Oilfield Wind Power
summary: China's CNOOC switched on Haiyou Anlan, the world's first 16-megawatt turbine on a tension-leg floating platform, in 136-metre water off Guangdong. It is expected to generate 54 million kilowatt-hours a year, replacing about 15,000 cubic metres of fuel oil.

title: A Robotic Arm That Speaks Sign Language Is Bringing Classrooms to Deaf Kids
summary: Norah Kimathi, 22, co-founded ZeroBionic to build $350 robotic hands that translate a teacher's speech into sign language in real time. The hands are now in 78 Kenyan schools, and at one Nairobi school for the deaf, teachers are using them to build a database of technical signs that expands the language itself.

title: Zipline's Rwanda Drones Marked 10 Years With 3 Million Deliveries and a 51% Drop in Maternal Hemorrhage Deaths
summary: A decade after Rwanda bet on an untested drone startup, Zipline's autonomous fleet has logged over 3 million deliveries and 140 million autonomous miles worldwide. A peer-reviewed Wharton study found in-hospital deaths from postpartum hemorrhage fell 51% at hospitals the drones served, and clinics cut blood stock by 63% because resupply is now a flight away.

title: Android's Earthquake Alerts Now Cover More Than 200 Regions
summary: Google's earthquake warning system, which turns phones into a seismic sensor network, has expanded from 98 to more than 200 regions after sending over a billion alerts. Those few seconds of warning have already saved lives, and new alerts now show the epicenter and estimated magnitude to help people take action.

title: Royal Surrey Performed Its 10,000th Robotic-Assisted Surgery
summary: The NHS trust's robotics programme has grown from a handful of cases in 2009 to one of the UK's busiest, treating more than 1,500 patients in 2024 alone. Some patients now go home the next day instead of spending a week in hospital, freeing around 10 beds a day for others.

title: AI Helped Nigerian Strawberry Farmers Grow 40% More Fruit
summary: Through the SmartBerry project, Nottingham Trent University researchers used AI, sensors and edge computing to guide irrigation and spot plant stress on Nigerian strawberry farms. Yields rose 40%, post-harvest waste fell 15%, market-grade fruit jumped from 70% to 88%, and the farm's turnover nearly doubled.

title: Drone-Delivered Vaccines Reached 3.9 Million Nigerian Children Who Missed Routine Shots
summary: Cross River State's zero-dose project used Zipline drones and 160 field teams across nine local government areas to reach children in riverine and mountainous areas where roads made conventional delivery nearly impossible. Zipline's Africa CEO says zero-dose prevalence fell 36% in Cross River and 42% in Bayelsa.

title: An AI Fall-Prevention System Gave a Senior Living Community Its First Fall-Free Month
summary: United Zion Retirement Community rejected cameras, which residents saw as a dignity risk, and instead used Helpany's radar-based AI that learns each resident's baseline and flags fall risk before it strikes. Falls dropped 70% and the community logged its first-ever month without a single fall.

title: Two New Pharmacy Robots Dispense Medicine Four Times Faster Than a Person at NHS Hospitals
summary: Colchester and Ipswich hospitals have upgraded their pharmacy teams with robots that pick and dispense medication at super speed while checking expiry dates on every packet. Every item is still checked by a human eye before it reaches a patient, freeing staff to process more prescriptions safely.
source_name: East Suffolk & North Essex NHS Foundation Trust

title: AI Cut a Chinese City's District Heating Energy Waste by Over 10%
summary: In Changsha, a district heating operator serving 60,000 people ran an AI system through a full heating season to forecast demand and catch faults before they wasted energy. Electricity consumption fell by more than 10% and the heat needed dropped 7%, while residents stayed warm.

title: A Kentucky Farmer Planted 900 Acres of Corn Without Anyone in the Tractor Cab
summary: Quint Pottinger fitted a $70,000 Sabanto autonomy kit to a John Deere 6130E and planted 900 acres of corn autonomously this spring, after a 500-acre autonomous wheat planting last fall. He has since sold two large planters, two big tractors and a combine, returning nearly $500,000 in equipment capital to his eighth-generation farm.

title: One Blood Test Caught 6.5 Times More Cancers in the Largest US Trial of Its Kind
summary: In the largest interventional multi-cancer early detection trial in North America, 35,878 adults took GRAIL's Galleri blood test alongside standard screening, and cancer detection rose 6.5-fold. Seventy percent of the newly found cancers have no recommended screening at all, and one participant, Franklin Weingarten, 88, is cancer-free today after the test caught his bile duct cancer early.

title: An AI Recycling Robot Started Sorting Sarasota's Waste at 60 Picks a Minute
summary: A Glacier AI-powered robot joined the Circular Services plant in Sarasota, pulling aluminum cans and HDPE plastics off a line that processes 50 tons of recycling an hour. Glacier's robots already sort recycling for about 1 in 10 Americans, keeping valuable commodities out of landfills and easing the grind of line work.

title: A 15-Minute Blood Test and AI Helped a Hospital Rethink Sepsis Care
summary: Tampa General Hospital paired its Palantir-built Sepsis Hub with MeMed's 15-minute blood test that reads the immune response to tell bacterial infections from viral ones. In an 893-patient study, 26% more patients were safely reclassified as unlikely to have sepsis, cefepime use fell by a third, hospitalizations dropped 13%, and savings reached about $179,000 per 100 patients.

title: An Automated Plant in Italy Began Turning 19,200 Tonnes of Textile Waste Back Into Spinning Fiber
summary: IGERS inaugurated a new automated textile recycling plant near Novara that uses near-infrared optical sorters to identify pure cotton and wool fractions, then mechanically regenerates them into flakes and opened fibers for the spinning industry. The 8 million euro facility tracks every material stream digitally from buffering to final output.

title: Google's Medical AI Interviewed Real Patients in a First-of-Its-Kind Lancet Study
summary: In the first prospective real-world study of its kind, published in The Lancet, 98 patients at a Boston primary care clinic talked through their symptoms with Google's AMIE chatbot before urgent appointments, with a physician watching every chat. No conversation needed a safety stop, the AI's differential matched the final diagnosis 90% of the time, and doctors said its summaries helped them prepare in three-quarters of cases.

title: One in Five Americans Has Ridden in a Robotaxi, and 83% Say the Ride Changed Their Mind
summary: A Cox Automotive survey found about one in five Americans has now ridden in a driverless car, and among those riders 83% said their perception of autonomous vehicles improved. Sam Abuelsamid of Telemetry notes riders tend to walk away with a much better impression once they actually experience the technology.

title: An AI Coaching App Helped Hypertension Patients Take Control of Their Blood Pressure
summary: In a Rush University Medical Center study published in the Journal of General Internal Medicine, 425 patients added the free Nuna app, with its AI health coach and gamified reminders, to their hypertension care. Systolic blood pressure fell 13.6 mm Hg among users with uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension versus 9.0 among controls, and one in five participants brought their high blood pressure under control early in the study.

title: An AI Reading Tutor Nearly Quadrupled Struggling Readers' Odds of Catching Up
summary: Perry Township Schools in Indiana deployed the Project Read AI tutor, which listens to young children read aloud and gives sound-by-sound feedback, across four schools. Among the 520 students who started the year below benchmark, a student using the tutor 30 minutes a week had roughly a 68% chance of catching up, nearly four times the odds of one barely using it.

title: An AI That Reads Breast MRIs to Predict Cancer Recurrence Won FDA Clearance
summary: SimBioSys won FDA 510(k) clearance for TumorSight Risk, the first AI tool that estimates breast cancer recurrence risk from routine MRI scans, validated on 2,129 patients across multiple institutions. It needs no extra procedures or hardware, giving oncologists personalized five- and ten-year risk scores before surgery.

title: The First Treatment for Schizophrenia's Negative Symptoms Is a Smartphone App
summary: Click Therapeutics' Motivista became the first FDA-authorized treatment for the negative symptoms of schizophrenia, delivered as a 16-week smartphone program alongside standard care. In its phase 3 trial, patients improved 62 percent more than those using a control app.

title: A One-Step Rapid Syphilis Test Catches the Infection Earlier
summary: Penn State researchers built a one-step rapid syphilis test that detects the disease sooner by swapping gold nanoparticles for layered silver-and-gold ones, producing test lines up to 46 percent stronger. Catching syphilis earlier means faster treatment and fewer clinic visits.

title: A Tongue-Controlled Exoskeleton Restored Hand Use After Spinal Cord Injury
summary: Researchers in Denmark and the Netherlands showed that five people with cervical spinal cord injuries could steer a soft hand exoskeleton with their tongues, restoring grasping for daily tasks like holding a bottle or a toothbrush. Participants reported high task success with low discomfort and fatigue.

title: Smart Sensors Are Watching Over 600 Elderly People Living Alone in Hefei
summary: In Hefei, China, door sensors and smoke detectors in the homes of more than 600 elderly residents now alert community workers when no activity is detected for 24 hours or an alarm trips. Around a dozen alerts a day get follow-up through a three-tier response of family, community workers and officials.

title: A Solar Desalination Box Is Keeping a Remote Aboriginal School Flowing
summary: Murdoch University's solar-powered desalination unit, small enough to fit inside a shipping container, is now supplying a remote Aboriginal boarding school that the water grid cannot reach. It has delivered more than 7.5 megalitres of freshwater, with students helping keep the operating logs.

title: Water Droplets Wired Into Brain-Like Networks Compute With Ions, Not Electrons
summary: Penn State engineers built soft networks of water droplets that process information like brain tissue, using ions instead of electrons at a far lower energy cost. In early tests, connected droplet networks cut prediction error by nearly half compared with isolated ones.

title: The First Engineered Geothermal Plant Is Now Selling Power to the Grid
summary: Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Utah became the first greenfield enhanced geothermal project anywhere to synchronize to the grid and enter commercial operation, with its first 33-megawatt block now earning revenue. A second 400-megawatt phase is already under construction.

title: Free All-Terrain Wheelchairs Opened Utah's National Park Trails to Everyone
summary: The National Park Service is now offering free all-terrain wheelchairs at Zion, Bryce, Canyonlands, Arches and Capitol Reef, opening unpaved trails to visitors with limited mobility. The balloon-tired chairs handle sand, rocks and ledges on a first-come, first-served basis.

title: Five Deaf Schoolgirls Built an AI App for Menstrual Health and Reached a Global Final
summary: Five deaf schoolgirls from Abuja, Nigeria, became global finalists at the 2026 Technovation Girls World Summit with Saving Pad, an AI-powered app that maps nearby sanitary pad banks and tracks supplies. They have already piloted it across three special schools, with plans to expand nationwide.

title: Battery Waste Became Pouch Cells That Last Nearly Twice as Long
summary: Researchers at Worcester Polytechnic Institute turned mixed battery waste into upgraded cathodes and graphite anodes, then built full pouch cells from nothing but the upcycled materials. The cells held 70% of their capacity after 2,590 cycles, nearly double the life of cells made with commercial materials, in research published in Advanced Energy Materials.

title: The World's First Purpose-Built Offshore Carbon Storage Platform Is Installed
summary: Eni CCUS Holding installed the Douglas platform in Liverpool Bay, the first offshore platform built specifically for carbon capture and storage serving industrial decarbonization. As the hub of the HyNet cluster, it will funnel CO2 captured from factories across North West England and North Wales into depleted gas reservoirs for permanent storage.

title: 47 Randomized Trials Find AI Tools Lift Student Achievement
summary: Researchers pooled 47 randomized controlled trials and found AI interventions raised academic achievement with a medium-to-large effect, roughly the size of some of the best conventional teaching programs. Gains leveled off after about 23 hours of use, a handy guide for schools deploying the tech thoughtfully.

title: FDA Clears an AI That Cuts False Alarms From Implantable Heart Monitors
summary: The FDA granted 510(k) clearance to Implicity's cloud-based AI analyzer, a manufacturer-agnostic second layer that re-checks alerts from implantable cardiac monitors made by Abbott, Biotronik, Boston Scientific and Medtronic. Published research shows it cut false-positive episodes by up to 76% while keeping high sensitivity for real events, easing the review burden on cardiac care teams.

title: Automated Insulin Delivery Wins FDA Clearance for Type 2 Diabetes
summary: Sequel Med Tech won FDA clearance to extend its twiist automated insulin delivery system to adults with type 2 diabetes, a population the company estimates at 5.5 million insulin users in the US. The pharmacy-dispensed pump pairs with popular continuous glucose monitors and continuously adjusts basal insulin using the Tidepool Loop algorithm.

title: A Nigerian Bionic Arm Matched to Black Skin Tones Lands on TIME's Best Inventions List
summary: The Ubokobong Bionic Arm pairs muscle-controlled movement with a hyper-realistic look designed for Black amputees, and it is already in use by clients in 56 countries. It grew from two brothers' own experience after one lost his fingers in a fireworks accident and could not find a prosthetic that matched his skin tone.

title: A Thought-Controlled Bionic Arm Moved Into Its First Real Home
summary: Alexander 'Avi' Davidson is the first person to use the University of Utah's nerve-interfaced bionic arm unsupervised at home, steering the hand with his thoughts and feeling touch through it. Within days he was writing, playing cards, making a sandwich, and holding his wife's hand while feeling the pressure back.

title: In England, 1,000 Companion Robots Are Helping Older People Live Independently
summary: Vera Gadsdon, 74, is one of more than 1,000 people across England now using Cera's Genie companion robots, which remind residents to eat, drink, and take medication while keeping them company between carer visits. Trials showed a 96% success rate in prompting the right medication at the right time.

title: A Tactile Tablet Lets Blind Fans Feel Live Sports Action
summary: OneCourt's tablet turns real-time player and ball tracking data into vibrations, so blind and low-vision fans can follow the game with their fingertips. Named to TIME's 2026 Best Inventions list, it was used at Super Bowl 60, where fans felt the ball's movement as it happened.

title: Wallpaper That Generates Electricity From Room Humidity Powered a Keyboard
summary: Binghamton University engineers built wallpaper from 1,596 tiny moisture-electric generators that turn indoor humidity into a steady current, enough to power a wireless keyboard. The paper also evens out room humidity as it works, and the team designed it to be printable for mass production.

title: A Surgical Robot That Lets Surgeons Feel Tissue Operated in a UK First
summary: Surgeons at St Thomas' Hospital in London used new Force Feedback instruments on a da Vinci 5 robot for the first time in the UK, letting them feel tissue resistance through the console controls. The first patient, 57-year-old Nicholas Kokkinos, was up and moving a day after his hernia repair with barely noticeable incision pain.
source_name: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust

title: The FDA Approved the First Heart Valve That Grows With Children
summary: The FDA approved Edwards Lifesciences' Autus valve on October 1, the first heart valve designed to expand as a child grows, from 13 mm up to adult size via a balloon catheter. In a 62-patient trial every child was free of device complications at 30 days, and the polymer leaflets could spare kids from repeat open-heart surgeries.

title: Europe Sold a Record 600,000 EVs in September
summary: Europeans bought nearly 600,000 electric vehicles in September, a monthly record up 39% from a year earlier, with the UK, France, Spain, Portugal and Finland all posting their best months ever. Battery electrics did the heavy lifting, jumping 50% year over year.

title: New England's Wind Power Hit Record After Record This Fall
summary: Wind turbines in New England generated 68% more electricity in the first nine months of 2026 than the same period last year, with September output more than doubling year over year. Nine months of wind power already beat all of 2025's total.

title: A Smart Ring Won FDA Clearance to Track Blood Pressure Without a Cuff
summary: The FDA cleared Happy Health's smart ring for continuous blood pressure monitoring with no cuff and no calibration, validated against arterial-line measurements with under 1 mmHg mean error. It builds on the ring's existing clearance for at-home sleep apnea diagnosis.

title: An AI Tool That Helps Diagnose Autism in Toddlers Won FDA Clearance
summary: The FDA cleared Argus Cognitive's Neurora, software that measures over 100 vocal, facial and gaze biometrics from a standard behavioral assessment to support autism diagnosis in children as young as 18 months. With autism affecting 1 in 31 US children and median diagnosis near age 4, earlier objective evidence could get kids help sooner.

title: Blind Veterans Ran a 10-Miler With AI Glasses, and Now Every Blind Veteran Gets a Pair Free
summary: Eight runners including blind Army veterans Roosevelt Morring, Rob Sanchas and Shawntina Gibson finished the Army Ten-Miler in heavy rain wearing Meta AI glasses that described the world around them. Meta committed to giving free Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses to every blind veteran in America, more than 130,000 people.

title: A Water-Based Battery Glue Could Make Lithium Batteries Easier to Recycle
summary: UC San Diego engineers created a fluorine-free battery binder from two cheap polymers linked with citric acid, replacing toxic solvents with plain water. Batteries built with it matched conventional performance, held capacity longer, and the electrodes could be recycled by simply soaking them in water.

title: A New Catalyst Gave Rechargeable Zinc-Air Batteries 300 Hours of Runtime
summary: Chemists at TU Darmstadt built a nickel-iron-carbon catalyst that let rechargeable zinc-air batteries survive 500 charge cycles. Since zinc-air can theoretically store five times the energy of lithium-ion, the advance revives a chemistry long stuck as single-use.

title: Wood Waste Made Lithium Batteries Safer and 60% Longer-Lasting
summary: Michigan State engineers turned lignin, a cheap wood waste from paper mills, into a battery separator that withstands heat three times better than plastic. Batteries using it lasted 60% longer in testing, a step toward taming lithium-ion fire risk.

title: A Hornbill Made History With the World's First Double 3D-Printed Beak
summary: A young southern ground hornbill at Amsterdam's Artis Zoo broke both his upper and lower beak, leaving him unable to eat or preen. Vets at Utrecht University fitted him with two custom 3D-printed titanium prostheses, and he was picking up food with his new beak the very next morning.

title: J&J's OTTAVA Becomes the First Table-Integrated Surgical Robot to Win FDA Authorization
summary: After an 11-year development journey, Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA system earned FDA market authorization for 10 general surgery procedures including gastric bypass. The design stows its robotic arms inside the operating table itself, freeing up space around the patient and tightening surgical workflows.

title: A New Wireless Power System Keeps Stretchy Medical Implants Running in a Moving Body
summary: South Korean researchers built a stretchable liquid-metal receiver that keeps implants powered even as the body twists and deforms. In animal tests it ran a soft cardiac pacemaker reliably, a step toward implants that conform to living tissue without wires.

title: Gene Therapy Gave Deaf Children Their Hearing Back.
summary: A one-time gene therapy infusion restored meaningful hearing in 9 of 12 children with profound inherited deafness, no implants required. One three-year-old went from near-total deafness to hearing in the normal range within weeks.

title: America Passed 80,000 Public Fast-Charging Ports
summary: America passed 80,000 public fast-charging ports after 4,106 were added in a single quarter, 73% of new ports at 250 kW or more, with a record 17.6 million charging sessions in July.

title: Tanzania Brought School to 751 Children With Disabilities
summary: Tanzania's new inclusive education strategy brought schooling to 751 children with disabilities through home- and hospital-based learning, 440 laptops and tablets, over 522,000 Braille and large-print books, and compulsory sign-language training for student teachers.

title: A Wearable Robot Helped ALS Patients Walk Farther
summary: A Toho University study found 30 ALS patients walked nearly 12 meters farther in a two-minute test after training with the Hybrid Assistive Limb, a wearable robot that reads faint muscle signals to amplify the wearer's own intended movement, while quality of life stayed stable.

title: Record Quarter for US Clean Power as 17.1 GW Came Online
summary: 164 utility-scale clean energy projects came online in the US in a single quarter, up 45% on the year, pushing total clean capacity to about 388 gigawatts. The quarter included SunZia, the largest land-based wind project in American history.

title: An Autonomous AI Triaged Skin Cancer Referrals Across Two UK Hospitals
summary: A CE-marked AI autonomously discharged 25 to 31% of urgent suspected skin cancer referrals across two UK hospitals, 8,391 patients, saving 2,851 clinician hours. The first large-scale real-world autonomous AI deployment in a cancer pathway.

title: GM Started Shipping EVs With Fully Recycled Battery Cells
summary: GM's closed-loop pilot turned 80 end-of-life battery packs into cathode material with 100% recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese, certified to match virgin material, and the first EVs carrying those cells are now shipping to customers.

title: Two Humanoid Robots Joined a Live Packaging Line in Korea
summary: CJ Logistics put two dual-arm humanoids to work stuffing cushioning into boxes at a fulfillment center, the first live logistics humanoid deployment in South Korea.

title: AI Eye Screening in Primary Care Halved the Cost of Catching Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: Autonomous AI eye screening in a Canadian primary-care clinic completed 93.6% of exams on the spot and cut the cost per diagnosed case of diabetic retinopathy roughly in half.

title: A Smartphone App Guided Blind Users 13% Faster With 41% Fewer Bumps
summary: Harvard's Mobilio smartphone app, with pedestrian-view AI and personalized audio cues, guided 14 blind and low-vision participants 13% faster with 41% fewer bumps, at reliability comparable to a human guide.

title: A Double Neural Bypass Rewired a Paralyzed Man's Nervous System.
summary: Keith Thomas, completely paralyzed since 2020, regained hand movement and wrist sensation through brain implants paired with AI-decoded stimulation. Remarkably, the gains persisted more than two years after stimulation stopped.

title: A Prosthetic Hand That Learns Each Amputee's Unique Muscle Signals
summary: A 3D-scanned, 3D-printed sleeve with magnetic sensors plus individualized AI decoded 19 hand gestures in real time for ten participants, including three amputees. It stayed accurate after 7,500 force cycles.

title: A 5.5-Pound Hip Exoskeleton Cut Stroke Survivors' Walking Effort by 18%
summary: A portable hip exoskeleton offloaded about 30% of hip work for stroke survivors with hemiparesis, cutting walking effort 18%. Some gait gains persisted after the device came off.

title: Trimming a Rice Gene Lifted Yields 25% and Drought Tolerance
summary: Chicago scientists trimmed a section of rice's own ALKBH9 and ALKBH10 genes, no foreign DNA, and boosted harvests 20 to 25% with better drought and heat tolerance. Published in Nature Genetics.

title: The World Installed a Record 664 GW of Solar in 2025.
summary: The world installed a record 664 gigawatts of solar in 2025, pushing the global fleet past 3 terawatts, triple its size four years ago. Solar now supplies about 9% of all electricity generated on Earth.

title: A Resistance Robot Taught Kids With SMA to Stand Up on Their Own
summary: A 2.1-pound knee robot that resists rather than assists movement helped six children with spinal muscular atrophy gain 130% quadriceps strength. All of them can now rise from a chair unassisted.

title: A Humanoid Robot Helped Build 30,000 BMWs Over an 11-Month Run
summary: A Figure 02 humanoid worked 10-hour shifts at BMW's Spartanburg plant inserting sheet-metal parts for welding at better than 99% accuracy per shift, helping build 30,000 cars over an 11-month run.

title: AI Thermal Imaging and Drones Now Guard Kenya's Wildlife Parks
summary: The Kenya Wildlife Service embedded AI thermal imaging, drones, and EarthRanger into daily ranger operations, with real-time poacher alerts across its parks.

title: The World Installed a Record 112 GW of Grid Batteries in 2025.
